scope: Exact coordinator/collector combination and concrete failure/argument paths; no native qualification
source_findings: Capture is bound to the live coordinator PID and /proc start_ticks before the native child, and the returned record is checked against that exact pair.
Each target has an independent collector; original bounded_process retains/reaps its direct group leader after final process-group kill, and native arguments after argv[0] remain exact.
Cargo JSON identifies one exact default release example source/artifact; actual launch is a hash-named byte-identical copy in the same examples directory, with pre/post SHA256 and inode checks.

The unchanged collector matches the expected crate/hash basename and exact --work-expensive-v1 selector; native main consumes args().skip(1), and the reviewed example does not use argv[0]/current_exe for source or material selection.

Per target success requires one actual executing-image record, exact build SHA, exact launch path/device/inode, coordinator PID/start_ticks, both subtree and post-open verification flags, exact selector, and retained-image readback SHA.
Native and reader failures preserve stdout/stderr and set process/component/report failure; missing/ambiguous/mismatched capture cannot pass.
Original child limits remain 300 seconds with stdout 256MiB and stderr 1MiB; new external coordination limits are labelled separately.
limits: No native child, collector, original reader or Cargo was executed by this review.
Polling may miss short execution; absence is a rejection, not inferred execution credit.
The legacy observed_selected_tests field denotes one CLI selector here, not a count of Rust tests.
If collector finish reports an alive thread, it remains a failed/incomplete capture; no stable complete-image claim is justified.
Prelaunch 23 checks were read as peer evidence, not rerun or attributed to this review.
